name: Factory Droid
disclaimer: Written from the documented interface, not verified against an install. Flags drift; correct and open a PR.

stdin.note: Verified from the droid exec overview (docs.factory.ai/cli/droid-exec/overview), read 2026-09-17: its Pipe quickstart pipes the prompt to `droid exec` with no prompt argument.

file.note: Verified from the same overview and the CLI reference (docs.factory.ai/reference/cli-reference): -f, --file <path> reads the prompt from a file.

resume.note: exec resumes by --session-id and still takes a prompt; --fork <id> branches instead

file.note: As send: -f is an option of exec. Resuming with piped input is not documented, so resume declares no stdin.

options.trust_none_why: droid exec without --auto is documented as read-only by default, but no flag states it, so a reviewer's argv cannot prove it; --restrict-tools takes the tool ids an install lists with --list-tools. Ineligible for the reviewer role until that is verified against an install.
options.effort_note: under exec -r is --reasoning-effort; interactively -r is resume

--auto.why: An autonomy level, in place of --skip-permissions-unsafe, which skips every permission check: --auto medium lets a droid exec turn edit files, install dependencies, build, test and commit locally, and a run that needs more stops with an error instead of asking. Read on 2026-09-17 from docs.factory.ai/cli/droid-exec/overview and docs.factory.ai/reference/cli-reference.
